concepts.name: fine-tuning adaptation
concepts.definition: Fine-tuning is the process of adapting a pre-trained language model to a specific task by updating its internal parameters using task-specific training data.
concepts.evidence: Fine-tuning actually changes the model's internal parameters

concepts.name: pre-training stage
concepts.definition: Pre-training is the initial, resource-intensive stage where a language model is trained on a large corpus of text data to learn general language patterns.
concepts.evidence: The first step is called pre-training. So this is the most expensive and one-time step

concepts.name: fine-tuning decision criteria
concepts.definition: Fine-tuning should be considered only when a task requires new behavior or writing style and sufficient training data or GPU resources are available.
concepts.evidence: If it doesn't need external knowledge, but needs new behavior or writing scale. Then you need to ask yourself another question, do you have training data, or do you have enough budget to use all these GPU resources?

concepts.name: fine-tuning stages
concepts.definition: The three stages of model development are pre-training, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and alignment, with SFT and alignment being the focus for AI practitioners.
concepts.evidence: we typically start from stage two... stage three is alignment

concepts.name: parameter efficient fine-tuning
concepts.definition: A fine-tuning method that updates only a small subset of model parameters (low-rank updates) to reduce computational cost and risk of catastrophic forgetting.
concepts.evidence: You can find you a relatively small model in a single computer GPU using LoRA parameter efficient fine-tuning

concepts.name: catastrophic forgetting
concepts.definition: A failure mode where a model loses previously learned knowledge after fine-tuning, overfitting to new training data.
concepts.evidence: This means after tuning, the model doesn't remember what it needs to stay before it fine-tuning

concepts.name: low-rank matrix decomposition
concepts.definition: A technique that approximates a large matrix by decomposing it into two smaller matrices whose product reconstructs the original matrix.
concepts.evidence: decomposed this matrix into two smaller ones

concepts.name: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
concepts.definition: A method that fine-tunes large models by updating only low-rank matrices instead of the full weight matrices.
concepts.evidence: we approximate the delta w using two small metrics

concepts.name: rank hyperparameter R
concepts.definition: A tunable parameter in LoRA that controls the dimensionality of the low-rank matrices and thus the number of trainable parameters.
concepts.evidence: the rank R is a very important hyper parameter you can control

concepts.name: LoRA inference addition
concepts.definition: During LoRA inference, the original and LoRA-modified weights are added together to produce the final output.
concepts.evidence: We just add them together during LoRA inference

concepts.name: LoRA hyperparameter tuning strategy
concepts.definition: A staged approach to tune LoRA parameters by first optimizing the learning rate, then adjusting the rank to improve performance.
concepts.evidence: You can start with some default values... tune the learning rate first... then adjust rank

concepts.name: LoRA rank efficiency
concepts.definition: LoRA can achieve competitive performance with very small rank values, such as rank 1 or 2, requiring tuning of only a few parameters.
concepts.evidence: LoRA already performs competitively with a very small like even R equals one or two

concepts.name: Quantization
concepts.definition: Quantization is the process of reducing the precision of model weights from higher bit representations (e.g., 16-bit or 32-bit) to lower bit representations (e.g., 4-bit) to decrease model size while attempting to preserve precision.
concepts.evidence: The core idea of quantization is quite simple

concepts.name: ABS max quantization
concepts.definition: ABS max quantization scales all weights to a range between the minimum and maximum absolute values, then maps them into discrete buckets to represent the weights in lower precision (e.g., 4-bit).
concepts.evidence: So in quantization this is one type of quantization mechanism called ABS max

concepts.name: Pitching optimizer
concepts.definition: Pitching optimizer is a mechanism that moves data not currently needed for computation from GPU memory to CPU memory during training to avoid GPU overload and save memory.
concepts.evidence: pitched optimizer will shift from those do not needed during the disk step of training

concepts.name: Instruction tuning
concepts.definition: Instruction tuning is a supervised fine-tuning process that trains a pre-trained model to follow human instructions by learning from instruction-response pairs.
concepts.evidence: instruction tuning or SFT is trained the model on the instruction on response pairs

concepts.name: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
concepts.definition: Supervised fine-tuning is a method to transform a pre-trained base model into one that follows human instructions by training on labeled instruction-response data.
concepts.evidence: supervised fine tuning or SFT address would to train the model to do

concepts.name: Base model behavior
concepts.definition: A base model, trained only on raw pre-training data, tends to perform text completion rather than instruction-following due to its training objective.
concepts.evidence: the base model actually did not answer the question. So instead of that, it would be that it just do a text completion

concepts.name: supervised fine-tuning limitations
concepts.definition: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has four key limitations: label quality ceiling, no notion of preference, inability to learn from feedback, and objective misalignment.
concepts.evidence: four key limitations

concepts.name: alignment training goal
concepts.definition: Alignment training aims to teach the model human values such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty to better align with user expectations.
concepts.evidence: goal of the alignment is to teach the model human values

concepts.name: objective misalignment in SFT
concepts.definition: Objective misalignment occurs in SFT because the loss function minimizes cross-entropy but does not ensure the model is helpful, honest, or safe.
concepts.evidence: objective misalignment

concepts.name: alignment in RLHF
concepts.definition: Alignment in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is the process of training a model to align its outputs with human preferences and values.
concepts.evidence: we want our model to have the same value as human preference

concepts.name: reinforcement learning policy
concepts.definition: A reinforcement learning policy is a decision-making mechanism that selects actions based on probabilities to maximize cumulative reward.
concepts.evidence: Policy is the decision making mechanism like we, inside we have a probability model

concepts.name: reward function in RL
concepts.definition: A reward function assigns numerical values to actions or states to guide the agent toward desired behaviors by maximizing positive rewards and avoiding penalties.
concepts.evidence: when every time Mario gets coin, the reward is a plus one

concepts.name: reinforcement learning for LM alignment
concepts.definition: Reinforcement learning is used to align language models with human preferences by maximizing a reward function during generation.
concepts.evidence: we can learn from this process, this reinforcement learning process for LM alignment

concepts.name: reward model based on human preference
concepts.definition: A reward model is trained using human preference data to evaluate and guide the language model's output quality.
concepts.evidence: we will use human preference as a reward function here

concepts.name: collecting human preference data via comparisons
concepts.definition: Human preference data is collected by presenting pairs of answers to questions and selecting the preferred one, rather than assigning absolute scores.
concepts.evidence: Instead of giving an answer to each question, we will give each question to answers. One is a good one, one is a bad one

concepts.name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
concepts.definition: A training method where a language model learns to align with human preferences by optimizing a reward signal derived from human judgments.
concepts.evidence: this is called reinforcement learning from human feedback

concepts.name: Proximal Policy Optimization
concepts.definition: A reinforcement learning algorithm that optimizes a policy by limiting policy updates to avoid large deviations, used in RLHF for language models.
concepts.evidence: one popular way is called PPO, which is proximal policy optimization

concepts.name: Reward model in RLHF
concepts.definition: A model that predicts human preference scores, serving as the reward signal to guide the policy model's learning.
concepts.evidence: reward is the human preference

concepts.name: Direct Preference Optimization
concepts.definition: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a method for aligning language models that directly uses preference data pairs to infer rewards without requiring a separate reward model.
concepts.evidence: it directly using the preference data, the score of the pairs of preference data to get the reward

concepts.name: GRPO advantage estimation
concepts.definition: GRPO estimates the advantage by generating multiple responses, averaging them to create a value baseline, and using this baseline to avoid learning a separate value function.
concepts.evidence: you just generate multiple responses, average them, then use that average as a value baseline

concepts.name: Memory efficiency in DPO
concepts.definition: DPO reduces memory requirements during training by only needing two models: the original model and the model being trained, instead of four models required by PPO.
concepts.evidence: DPO only needs two, the original model and the model to be trained

concepts.name: Quantization
concepts.definition: Quantization is a process of reducing the numerical precision of a model's parameters to decrease its size while attempting to preserve performance.
concepts.evidence: Quantization is a process of reducing the numerical precision of a model with and activities.

concepts.name: Post-training quantization
concepts.definition: Post-training quantization applies quantization to a pre-trained model after standard training, using data to compute quantization parameters before inference.
concepts.evidence: This is, we will do the same thing with pre-trained model, train, do the SFT and alignment. Then we get a model. After this, we will do, we will use some data to compute the quantization method, then quantize the network and run inference.

concepts.name: Quantization aware training
concepts.definition: Quantization aware training integrates quantization objectives directly into the model training process to account for quantization noise and improve accuracy.
concepts.evidence: That means we simultaneously do quantization and find meaning at the same time.

concepts.name: knowledge distillation benefits
concepts.definition: Knowledge distillation produces smaller student models that run faster with only a small performance loss compared to the original teacher model.
concepts.evidence: 40% smaller, 60% faster, 97% of performance

concepts.name: mixture of experts
concepts.definition: A model architecture where only a subset of specialized sub-networks (experts) is activated per input, improving efficiency and scalability.
concepts.evidence: only one of several experts are actually activated

concepts.name: sparse vs dense activation
concepts.definition: Sparse activation models activate only a small subset of parameters per input, unlike dense models that activate all parameters.
concepts.evidence: only activate a small subset of network

concepts.name: Prompt engineering method
concepts.definition: Prompt engineering is a simple, free approach to quickly obtain results by crafting input prompts for large language models.
concepts.evidence: start from a simplest method... prompt engineering, maybe the first, because it's free and you get instant results

concepts.name: Supervised fine-tuning with LoRA/QLoRA
concepts.definition: Supervised fine-tuning using LoRA or QLoRA adjusts model behavior such as writing style or reasoning when data is available.
concepts.evidence: if you need behavior changes... SFT using LoRA or QLoRA might be a choice. Condition is you have the data.

concepts.name: Direct Preference Optimization
concepts.definition: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is an alignment method that directly uses data for reward estimation without a separate reward model.
concepts.evidence: DPO is a better choice than PPO because it has less models to handle. And it directly use your data to do the reward estimation.

concepts.name: Project submission components
concepts.definition: A project submission must include a user manual explaining installation and execution, and optionally source code and API key instructions if external APIs are used.
concepts.evidence: give a self-explanatory written about how to install, how to run it

concepts.definition: The quiz will be on-site using the Examiner system, consisting mainly of multiple-choice questions covering topics introduced in the second half of the course.
concepts.evidence: the quiz will be in the similar format as the midterm quiz, it will be on site using the examiner

concepts.name: Mock test preparation
concepts.definition: Students are advised to test the new quiz system using a mock test before the actual quiz to avoid technical issues.
concepts.evidence: I will recommend you to test using the mock test to test your system first before you come in
